acceptance_criteria: Confirm implementation matches lib/letflow/design/iss0276-dev-bootstrap-seed.md's resolved decisions (attrs shape, idempotency handling, LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED non-handling)

PASS or FAIL with itemized issues if FAIL

result.summary:
Reviewed lib/mix/tasks/letflow.seed.ex against lib/letflow/design/iss0276-dev-bootstrap-seed.md, the lib/mix/tasks/letflow.copy_identity_tables.ex precedent, and docs/anti-patterns.md. PASS, no issues.

1. Design conformance -- exact match, no undisclosed deviation. @attrs literal (§2 step 2) is byte-identical to the design's map. Call sequence (§2 steps 1-6) is followed in order: Mix.Task.run("app.start") first line, create_tenant/1, then provision_tenant_schema/1 -> replay_migrations/1 via the provision_and_replay/2 helper, success message naming tenant id + migration count. LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED handling (§3): correctly NOT special-cased in the task -- inherited automatically via app.start's existing Letflow.Repo.init/2 guard, exactly as designed; confirmed no System.get_env call anywhere in the file. Idempotency (§4): {:error, :duplicate_slug} branch calls resolve_tenant_by_realm("bpm-default"); {:ok, tenant} continues to provision_and_replay with verb "already present, re-provisioned/re-verified"; {:error, :not_found} raises naming the genuine slug-collision case, not silently proceeding -- matches §4 exactly, including the two distinct success-message verbs from §4's last bullet. Error handling (§5): provision_tenant_schema/1 and replay_migrations/1 failures both hit Mix.raise/1 with tenant id + inspect(reason); create_tenant/1's changeset-error branch also raises with inspect(changeset.errors) -- matches. README addition (§7): verified via git diff main...HEAD -- README.md -- placed exactly where specified (after the ecto.setup/mix run block, before the curl health-check block), fenced LETFLOW_DEV_DB_CONFIRMED=1 mix letflow.seed command plus one prose paragraph naming resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 and AuthPipeline, idempotency, and the fresh-DB/ecto.reset trigger condition -- content matches §7's specified prose near-verbatim. No new top-level README section added, per §7's own constraint.

2. Exhaustiveness check (beyond what the design narrated): independently read Letflow.Identity.create_tenant/1's @spec (lib/letflow/identity.ex:582-583) -- its full return type is {:ok, Tenant.t()} | {:error, :duplicate_slug} | {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()}, and the task's outer case has exactly those three clauses, so no unmatched-clause CaseClauseError is possible. resolve_tenant_by_realm/1 and the two TenantProvisioning calls are handled via nested case/2-clause matches with a generic {:error, reason} catch-all fallthrough on the provisioning steps, which is a defensible superset of the design's per-atom enumeration in §5 (broader than named, not narrower) -- no gap.

3. Scope -- clean. git diff --stat main...HEAD shows exactly one new lib file (lib/mix/tasks/letflow.seed.ex), the README.md addition, the new design doc, and this run's own handoff/log/registry bookkeeping -- nothing else under lib/ or priv/ touched. No new Ecto schema, migration, behaviour, or generic plumbing introduced ahead of what ISS-0276 needs -- the task is a thin sequential wrapper over three pre-existing, already-reviewed functions, same shape as the copy_identity_tables precedent's 'thin wrapper' framing. No scope-creep abstractions.

4. Idiom vs. copy_identity_tables.ex precedent -- matches: @shortdoc, @moduledoc with a ## Usage section, use Mix.Task, @impl Mix.Task, Mix.Task.run("app.start") as run/1's first line, Mix.shell().info/1 on success, Mix.raise/1 on every failure branch, no arguments/options. One addition beyond the precedent -- an explicit @spec run(args :: [String.t()]) :: :ok -- is not scope creep: the design (§1) explicitly specifies that typespec, and it is a stricter, still-idiomatic addition consistent with @spec usage elsewhere in this codebase, not an undisclosed deviation.

5. docs/anti-patterns.md -- no applicable entry. The entries on file concern ORCH bookkeeping/timestamp/rebase/id-collision hazards, an Ecto fragment/1 SQL-literal duplication pattern, and toolchain/Docker verification notes -- none apply to this single new Mix.Task file. No new anti-pattern found worth logging from this review.

Supervision (question 2 of REVIEWER's charter) is not applicable here: this is a one-shot Mix.Task CLI process, not a supervised runtime component: it creates no new process, spawns nothing, and does not touch Letflow.InstanceSupervisor or any instance-isolation path.

Type-safety gaps (question 3): none found -- the task adds no new transition/state logic of its own; it only sequences three already-typed function calls whose own return types are already @spec'd and exhaustively matched.
